name: Azure AI Vision Read OCR (Computer Vision)
price_note: As of 2026-06: Free tier (F0) = 5,000 transactions/month, capped at 20 calls/min (also limited to first 2 pages of PDF/TIFF and 4 MB file size). Standard tier (S1) OCR/Read = approx. $1.00 per 1,000 transactions for the 0-1M/month volume tier, with volume discounts at higher tiers (commonly cited around $1.50/1,000 in some regions/older quotes; verify current per-region price on the Azure pricing page, which lists OCR/Read under "OCR (Read)"). One transaction = one image; for documents, page-based billing applies. On-premises Docker container billing follows the same Standard transaction model (requires a billable Azure resource for metering).
best_for: Cloud applications already on Azure that need reliable printed-text (and some handwritten) extraction from images and PDFs across many languages, with bounding boxes and confidence scores - especially real-time UX scenarios (Read 4.0) or batch document processing (Document Intelligence Read).

name: Calamari OCR
price_note: Free and open source (no paid tier, no hosted service). As of 2026-06: zero cost; only your own compute (CPU/GPU). Pretrained models are free downloads.
best_for: Digital-humanities and library/archive projects doing high-accuracy transcription of printed and historical documents (especially Latin-script Antiqua/Fraktur) where you can pre-segment lines and want a free, trainable, fully local engine — often as the recognition backend inside OCR4all or eScriptorium.

name: Camelot
price_note: Free and open source (MIT), no usage fees or quotas. As of 2026-06. Self-hosted; only your own compute costs apply (GPU optional for the [ml] Table Transformer backend).
best_for: Extracting tabular data from born-digital, text-based PDFs (financial reports, government/tender filings, scientific papers, manuals) into pandas DataFrames or CSV/JSON/Excel — especially tables with visible gridlines (lattice). Best when you need a free, offline, scriptable tool with quality metrics, and can tune parameters per document type.

name: DeepSeek-OCR
price_note: Free, open-weights (MIT). No first-party hosted API or per-page price; the only cost is your own GPU compute. Paper cites throughput of ~200k+ pages/day on a single A100-40G. As of 2026-06, third-party hosts (Hugging Face inference providers, Replicate, API aggregators) may charge to serve it, but there is no official DeepSeek OCR endpoint.
best_for: Large-scale, GPU-backed document-to-markdown/text conversion where you want an open, self-hostable model with strong structured output (tables, math, charts) and excellent token-efficiency — e.g., building LLM training corpora or on-prem document pipelines.

name: Docling
price_note: Free and open-source (MIT). No usage fees. As of 2026-06 the only costs are your own compute/GPU. Models (layout, TableFormer, GraniteDocling VLM, EasyOCR/RapidOCR weights) download once and are cached locally at no cost. Remote OCR backends it can wrap (e.g. Apple Vision on macOS, or a KServe inference server you host) are themselves free; any third-party paid OCR would be billed separately by that provider.
best_for: Self-hosted, privacy-sensitive document-to-structured-content conversion at scale: converting PDFs/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/HTML/images into clean Markdown or lossless JSON for RAG and gen-AI pipelines, with strong table, layout, formula, and code extraction. Best when you need pluggable OCR (swap Tesseract/EasyOCR/RapidOCR/Apple Vision) and full offline/air-gapped operation rather than a hosted API.

name: docTR
price_note: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); no license, subscription, or per-page fees. Only cost is your own compute/hosting. As of 2026-06. (Mindee also sells a separate commercial document-AI API, but docTR the library is free.)
best_for: Developers needing a free, self-hosted, privacy-preserving OCR pipeline for printed PDFs and document images, who want word-level text plus bounding boxes and confidence in structured JSON, and who value swappable detection/recognition models and Python integration over turnkey table/math/handwriting extraction.

name: dots.ocr
price_note: The model itself is free (MIT, open weights) — self-host with no licensing cost. There is no official first-party paid API; pricing comes only from third-party hosts (as of 2026-06): Replicate ~$0.0032 per run (community sljeff/dots.ocr deployment); Chutes lists it at ~$0.01 / 1M input tokens and ~$0.01 / 1M output tokens, pay-as-you-go with no subscription. Self-hosting cost is just GPU compute.
best_for: Self-hosted, cost-free, privacy-preserving end-to-end document parsing where you want one compact model to do layout detection, reading order, tables, formulas, and multilingual text extraction with structured JSON+bbox output — competitive with proprietary VLM OCR services without per-page fees.

name: EasyOCR
price_note: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); no usage fees, no API. Models download once at first use. As of 2026-06 there is no hosted/paid tier from Jaided AI for the library itself; Jaided AI offers separate paid custom-model training/enterprise support engagements (quote-based), not a metered OCR API.
best_for: Local, offline, multilingual extraction of text + bounding boxes from images and scene/photo text where a permissive license and zero per-page cost matter, and where tables/forms/math/structured layout are NOT required.

name: GOT-OCR2.0
license: Apache-2.0 (code and model weights); training data released CC-BY-NC-4.0
price_note: Free open-weights model (Apache-2.0). No first-party paid or hosted API. As of 2026-06 you self-host the ~580M-param weights and pay only your own compute. Third-party hosts (e.g. Clarifai listing under stepfun-ai/ocr, or community Replicate/fal-style endpoints) may charge per call, but those are unofficial and pricing varies by provider.
best_for: Teams needing a free, self-hosted, privacy-preserving single-model OCR for English/Chinese documents that also captures formulas, tables, charts and sheet music — especially academic PDFs, STEM/scientific content, and pipelines wanting LaTeX/markdown output without per-page API costs. Less suited to many-language production OCR or layout-rich document parsing where 2025-era specialists now lead.

name: img2table
price_note: Free and open-source (MIT) as of 2026-06. No cost for the library itself. Note: cloud OCR backends it can plug into (AWS Textract, Google Vision, Azure) are billed separately by those providers; local backends (Tesseract, PaddleOCR, EasyOCR, docTR, Surya, RapidOCR) are free.
best_for: Extracting structured tables (including merged cells and borderless layouts) from images and PDFs into pandas DataFrames or Excel, on CPU-only infrastructure, with freedom to pick any OCR backend (local or cloud). Good fit when you need a free, self-hosted, pluggable table extractor rather than a full document-understanding model.

name: InternVL (3 / 3.5)
license: Apache-2.0 (InternVL3.5); MIT (InternVL3). Note: variants built on Qwen2.5/Qwen3 inherit those base-model licenses (mostly Apache-2.0).
price_note: Free, open-weight models (no usage fees). As of 2026-06 you pay only your own compute/GPU cost to self-host. No official first-party hosted API or per-page price; third-party inference providers (e.g. OpenRouter, SiliconFlow) host some sizes at their own token rates.
best_for: Self-hosted, privacy-sensitive document/chart/screenshot understanding and OCR-plus-reasoning where you want a single open-weight VLM to read text AND answer questions, extract key-value pairs, parse tables/forms, and ground regions — not for high-volume, low-cost plain-text page transcription.

name: Keras-OCR
price_note: Free and open source (MIT). No fees, no API, no quotas. Only cost is local compute (GPU recommended for throughput). As of 2026-06.
best_for: Self-hosted, free English scene/printed-text detection+recognition where you want word-level bounding boxes and the option to fine-tune the detector or recognizer end-to-end on your own data, and where case/punctuation insensitivity and Latin-only output are acceptable.

name: Kraken
price_note: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); no license fee or per-page cost as of 2026-06. The engine, training pipeline, and the freely-licensed model repository are all free. Only real cost is self-provided compute: a Nvidia GPU with ~8GB+ VRAM is recommended for training generalized models from scratch, while fine-tuning and inference run on CPU (much slower). There is no official paid/hosted Kraken API; the closest "service" is a self-hosted or institution-hosted eScriptorium instance, which is itself free OSS.
best_for: Digitizing historical manuscripts and early printed books, and non-Latin / low-resource scripts (Arabic, Hebrew, Syriac, Greek, Indic, Fraktur), where you can train or fine-tune a custom model on your material. The default engine for digital-humanities and library/archive HTR workflows, especially via eScriptorium.

name: Llama 3.2 Vision (11B / 90B)
license: LLAMA-3.2-COMMUNITY (open-weight, not OSI-approved; commercial use allowed, >700M MAU clause)
price_note: Weights are free to download and self-host (compute is your cost). Hosted API (as of 2026-06): 90B Vision Instruct ~$0.72/1M blended (input and output both ~$0.72/1M) on AWS Bedrock, which is currently the main tracked first-party-ecosystem provider on Artificial Analysis; 11B Vision is cheaper (roughly $0.06-$0.35/1M depending on provider, e.g. ~$0.06/1M on AWS Bedrock, ~$0.18/1M historically on Groq). NOTE: Groq deprecated/decommissioned its Llama 3.2 Vision (11B/90B) preview endpoints on 2025-04-07 in favor of Llama 4 Scout, so Groq no longer serves these models. Prices are general LLM token prices; image tokens are billed within the same token budget. No per-page OCR pricing.
best_for: Teams that want an open-weight, self-hostable multimodal model for document understanding, chart/table reasoning, and English document-to-Markdown OCR where layout reasoning and Q&A matter more than character-perfect transcription — and who want to avoid sending data to a third party.

name: Marker (Datalab)
license: GPL-3.0-or-later (code); model weights under modified AI-Pubs OpenRAIL-M (free for research/personal/startups under $2M)
price_note: As of 2026-06: Self-hosted is free (GPLv3 code; weights free under the OpenRAIL-M revenue threshold). Hosted Datalab API: $5 free credits on signup; standard Marker/OCR conversion bills roughly $6 per 1,000 pages, LLM-mode structured extraction $25 per 1,000 pages for documents over 50 pages (and ~$6/1,000 pages with page_schema); spreadsheets billed by cells (simple mode capped at $0.60/sheet). EU processing adds +25%. Exact per-processor rates live on datalab.to/pricing and shift over time.
best_for: Converting whole PDFs and office/EPUB documents to clean Markdown/JSON/HTML at scale, preserving reading order, tables, equations (LaTeX), forms and references; strong for RAG ingestion pipelines where layout fidelity matters more than per-character OCR of a single image.

name: MinerU
license: MinerU Open Source License (Apache-2.0 based, with additional conditions; relicensed from AGPL-3.0 as of v3.1.0)
price_note: Self-hosted OSS is free. Hosted mineru.net API is in free beta (as of 2026-06): each account gets a high-priority parsing quota of 2000 pages/day, with reduced priority beyond that and no hard daily page cap; submit-task rate limit 300 req/min and up to 10,000 files/day (max 100 HTML). No published per-page list price; enterprise/custom limits via opendatalab@pjlab.org.cn. Third-party resellers (e.g. 302.AI) offer pay-as-you-go wrappers.
best_for: Converting complex PDFs, scanned documents, and Office files into clean, reading-order LLM/RAG-ready Markdown and structured JSON at scale — especially multilingual and math/table/chart-heavy scientific or business documents — either fully self-hosted (privacy) or via a free-beta hosted API.

name: MiniCPM-V (4.5 / 4.6)
price_note: Free open-weight model (Apache-2.0) for self-hosting; no per-token cost when run locally. As of 2026-06, OpenBMB also offers a hosted OpenAI-compatible API at https://api.modelbest.cn/v1 (released 2026-05-17) with a public free API key for MiniCPM-V 4.6 (models MiniCPM-V-4.6-Instruct and MiniCPM-V-4.6-Thinking). Paid-tier pricing and rate limits for the hosted API are not publicly documented.
best_for: On-device / privacy-sensitive document OCR and document understanding where you want a single open-weight model that handles high-resolution any-aspect images, tables, math, handwriting, charts, and even video — without per-page API costs. Strong choice when you need GPT-4o-class OCR locally on a laptop, a single mid-range GPU, or even a phone (4.6).

name: MMOCR
price_note: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). No license, subscription, or per-page fees. As of 2026-06, the only cost is your own compute/GPU. No hosted/managed API is offered by the project.
best_for: Researchers and ML engineers who want to train, fine-tune, benchmark, or compose state-of-the-art scene text detection / recognition / spotting / KIE models under a unified, modular, config-driven PyTorch framework - rather than teams wanting a turnkey document OCR product.

name: Nanonets
license: mixed (proprietary platform; open models: Nanonets-OCR-s & OCR2-3B under Qwen Research License (non-commercial), OCR2-1.5B-exp Apache-2.0)
price_note: As of 2026-06: Sign-up gives $200 prepaid credits (no card, credits never expire). Pay-as-you-go per block run by complexity: ~$0.02/run simple (format/route/export), ~$0.10/run standard AI (classify/validate), ~$0.30/run complex AI (extraction/genAI). A typical invoice workflow runs 4-6 blocks ~under $2/doc end-to-end. Growth (up to ~40% volume discount) and Enterprise are custom-quote. Separate free DocStrange cloud extraction tier: ~10,000 docs/month. Open-weight models on HuggingFace are free to self-host.
best_for: Teams needing no-code/low-code IDP for invoices, receipts, IDs, bank statements and AP automation with prebuilt + trainable custom models, confidence-scored field extraction, and many integrations; developers wanting LLM-ready markdown via API or self-hosted open VLM OCR models.

name: Nougat
price_note: Free and open source (MIT code). No hosted/paid API offered by Meta. Costs are self-hosted compute only (GPU recommended). As of 2026-06, weights remain CC-BY-NC-4.0, so commercial use of the released weights is restricted by license.
best_for: Converting born-digital or scanned English scientific/academic PDFs into Mathpix-Markdown (.mmd) with inline LaTeX math and tables — e.g. building markdown/LaTeX corpora from papers for RAG, search, or ML training where preserving equations matters.

name: OCR4all
price_note: Free and open-source under MIT license. No subscriptions, no paywalled features, no usage fees. Self-hosted, so the only cost is your own compute/hardware. (As of 2026-06.)
best_for: Libraries, archives, and digital-humanities researchers doing OCR/HTR of historical printings and manuscripts (15th–19th c.), especially when iterative model training and manual layout/text correction (via the LAREX editor) are needed for highest accuracy on challenging material — all on-premises and free.

name: ocrmac (Apple Vision)
price_note: Free and open-source (MIT). No usage fees of any kind — OCR runs on-device via Apple's Vision framework, which ships free with macOS. Only cost is owning a Mac. As of 2026-06.
best_for: Fast, free, fully on-device OCR of printed text from images on macOS — batch image-to-text pipelines, screenshot/photo text extraction, privacy-sensitive workloads where data must not leave the machine, and developers already on Apple Silicon who want word/line text plus confidence and bounding boxes without external services.

name: OCRopus / ocropy
price_note: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). No paid tier, no hosted service. Self-hosted only; you pay only for your own compute. As of 2026-06.
best_for: Historical and early-printed-book OCR pipelines where you train a custom line model per typeface/script, and academic/digital-humanities work that needs a transparent, fully local, trainable LSTM line recognizer. In practice, new projects should use its successors (Kraken, Calamari, OCR4all).

name: olmOCR
price_note: Free, open-source (Apache-2.0). No license/API fee. Self-hosted compute cost only: Ai2 reports ~$190-200 per 1,000,000 PDF pages (roughly $0.0002/page; "10,000 pages for less than $2" on a single H100 with FP8), about 1/32 the cost of GPT-4o batch API. As-of 2026-06. GPU rental/electricity is the real cost driver; there is no official hosted endpoint.
best_for: Large-scale, cost-efficient linearization of English PDFs (academic papers, historical scans, legal docs, multi-column reports, math/tables) into clean Markdown for LLM/RAG training corpora and document pipelines — when you have GPUs and want full local control and an open license.

name: OnnxTR
price_note: Free and open-source (Apache-2.0). No license fee, no API/usage cost — runs entirely on your own CPU/GPU. Pretrained ONNX weights are downloaded free from the Hugging Face Hub. Only cost is your own compute. As of 2026-06.
best_for: Production OCR on printed/scanned documents where you want docTR's quality but a lightweight, TensorFlow/PyTorch-free install with fast CPU inference (8-bit quantization, OpenVINO) or simple GPU/CoreML deployment — e.g. embedding OCR in containers, edge/CPU servers, or as a Docling OCR backend.

name: owocr
price_note: The owocr software is free and open-source (GPL-3.0); no license fee. Local engines (Apple Vision/Live Text, WinRT OCR, OneOCR, Chrome Screen AI, EasyOCR, RapidOCR, Manga OCR, meikiocr, NDLOCR-Lite) run at zero cost. Cloud backends bill on the user's own provider account if used: Google Vision and Azure Document Intelligence are pay-per-page; OCRSpace has a free tier plus paid plans; Google Lens and Bing are accessed without an API key. As of 2026-06, owocr itself adds no markup.
best_for: Real-time, on-screen Japanese text capture for language learning, manga, visual novels, and anime — and more broadly as a single Python/CLI facade that unifies native OS OCR (Apple Vision, Windows OCR/OneOCR), local libraries (EasyOCR, RapidOCR, Manga OCR), and cloud engines (Google Lens/Vision, Bing, Azure, OCRSpace) behind one interface.

name: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv5 / PaddleOCR-VL)
price_note: The toolkit and all models (PP-OCRv5/v6, PaddleOCR-VL, PP-StructureV3) are free and Apache-2.0 — self-hosting cost is just your own compute. Optional third-party hosted inference: e.g. Novita lists PaddleOCR-VL at ~$0.02 per 1M input and ~$0.02 per 1M output tokens (as of 2026-06); WaveSpeedAI ~ $0.005 per image. Baidu AI Studio / Qianfan also exposes a hosted PaddleOCR-VL API (Chinese-cloud pricing, region-dependent). No vendor-run free tier is documented for the hosted APIs; the free path is running the OSS models yourself.
best_for: High-accuracy multilingual document parsing and OCR where you want full control and zero per-page fees: self-hosted pipelines for printed/scene/handwritten text, tables, formulas and charts, with a choice between an ultra-lightweight CPU/edge pipeline (PP-OCRv5/v6) and a SOTA VLM (PaddleOCR-VL) for complex documents and LLM ingestion.

name: PaddleOCR 3.0 / PP-StructureV3
price_note: Software is free (Apache-2.0) to self-host; you pay only your own compute (GPU/CPU). Baidu AI Studio also offers a hosted PP-StructureV3 / PaddleOCR-VL API with a free community tier documented at up to ~20,000 pages/day; AI Studio paid/enterprise serving is credit/quote-based, not a published fixed per-page rate. As of 2026-06.
best_for: Self-hosted, free, high-accuracy parsing of complex multi-column PDFs/scans into Markdown/JSON with tables, formulas, charts and correct reading order — especially when Chinese/English or 100+ languages and on-prem privacy matter.

name: pix2tex / LaTeX-OCR
price_note: Free and open source (MIT). No usage fees, no API costs. Pretrained model checkpoints download automatically on first run. Only cost is your own compute. As of 2026-06.
best_for: Turning images/screenshots of a single printed mathematical equation into LaTeX, locally and for free — e.g. capturing formulas from PDFs/papers/websites into editable LaTeX via the screenshot GUI or batch via the Python API.

name: Qwen2-VL / Qwen2.5-VL / Qwen3-VL
license: Apache-2.0 (open weights); DashScope API is proprietary service
price_note: Open weights are free to self-host. Via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio / DashScope (International/Singapore endpoint, as of 2026-06): dedicated qwen-vl-ocr $0.07/M input, $0.16/M output tokens; qwen-vl-max $0.8/M in, $3.2/M out; qwen-vl-plus $0.21/M in, $0.63/M out; qwen3-vl-plus tiered $0.2-$0.6/M in, $1.6-$4.8/M out by context length; qwen3-vl-flash $0.05-$0.12/M in, $0.4-$0.96/M out. Images are billed by token count (roughly 256-1500+ tokens/image depending on resolution; qwen-vl-ocr caps at 30,000 tokens/image). China-mainland endpoint pricing differs (often lower).
best_for: Complex multilingual document parsing where layout, tables, formulas, charts, handwriting and structured extraction matter in one model — historical/scanned docs, receipts/forms (key-value), academic papers (LaTeX math), and web/mobile screenshots. Good when you want one self-hostable open-weight model instead of a classical OCR + layout pipeline, or a cheap hosted OCR endpoint (qwen-vl-ocr).

name: RapidOCR
price_note: Free and open-source (Apache-2.0). No usage fees, no API, no subscription. Only cost is your own compute. As of June 2026.
best_for: Fast, fully offline, privacy-preserving multilingual OCR (especially Chinese/CJK + English) embedded into applications across Python, C++, Java, C#, Android, iOS, and .NET without a Python/Paddle dependency. Ideal when you want PaddleOCR's accuracy but need lightweight ONNX Runtime deployment, edge/mobile inference, or non-Python integration.

name: Surya OCR
license: Apache-2.0 (code); modified AI Pubs Open RAIL-M (weights)
price_note: As of 2026-06: OSS self-host is free under the weights license (research/personal/startups under the funding+revenue threshold; commercial self-host needs a paid license — contact sales). Hosted Datalab API is pay-as-you-go priced per 1,000 pages per processor (OCR/Marker tiers roughly $1-4 per 1,000 pages; higher 'extract' tiers up to ~$25/1,000 pages for large docs), with $5 in free signup credits. EU processing +25%; data-retention or startup discounts of 25-33% available.
best_for: Self-hosted, multilingual document OCR with built-in layout, reading-order, table, and inline-math recognition — ideal when you want a small (650M) open model that runs on a single GPU or even a MacBook and produces structured JSON/HTML/Markdown output.

name: Microsoft Table Transformer (TATR)
price_note: Free and open-source (MIT). No service/API fees; you run the models yourself, so the only cost is your own compute/GPU. Model weights download free from Hugging Face. As of 2026-06.
best_for: Detecting tables and recovering their cell/row/column structure from PDFs and document images (especially scientific and financial reports), as a specialized stage in a document-extraction pipeline rather than a general OCR engine.

name: Tabula / tabula-py
price_note: Free and open source (MIT). No usage fees, no API, no quotas. As of 2026-06. Only "cost" is a local JVM (Java 8+) install.
best_for: Extracting tabular data from text-based (digitally generated) PDFs into pandas DataFrames or CSV/TSV/JSON — financial reports, government data dumps, scientific tables — in a scripted Python pipeline, free and on-prem.

name: Tesseract (pytesseract / tesserocr)
price_note: Free and open source (Apache-2.0). No usage fees, no API costs, no quotas. As of 2026-06, the only cost is your own compute. Python wrappers (pytesseract, tesserocr) are also free/OSS.
best_for: Local, free, offline OCR of clean printed/typed documents in many languages where data privacy or zero cost matters. A solid baseline/default for digitizing books, scanned PDFs, and forms; good when you control preprocessing. Not the right tool for handwriting, math, complex multi-column layouts, or table-structure extraction.

name: Texify / Surya (LaTeX OCR)
license: Apache-2.0 (Surya code); model weights under a modified AI-Pubs OpenRAIL-M (free for research, personal use, and orgs under $5M funding/revenue). Legacy texify: GPL-3.0 code, CC-BY-SA-4.0 weights.
price_note: Self-hosted OSS is free (subject to model license). Datalab hosted API is per-1,000-pages billing. Free monthly allowance ~$20/mo on a work email, ~$10/mo on a personal email, plus ~$5 free credits on card verification; no credit card required to start. Team plan is a fixed monthly fee (~$400 included usage) metered against the same rate card with pay-as-you-go overage. (As of 2026-06; check datalab.to/pricing for current per-processor rates.)
best_for: Converting math/equation images and PDFs to MathJax/KaTeX-renderable LaTeX + Markdown, locally and free, with full-page multilingual OCR, layout, and table extraction as part of the same pipeline; optionally offloaded to Datalab's hosted API for scale.

name: TrOCR
price_note: Free and open-source (model weights + Transformers library). No usage fees. As of 2026-06, the only cost is your own compute (CPU/GPU). Weights and code are MIT-licensed via the microsoft/unilm repo and Hugging Face Hub.
best_for: Recognizing the text content of pre-cropped single text-line images (printed or handwritten), especially English documents where you already have a line/word detector and want high-accuracy transformer-based recognition that runs fully offline.

name: TrOCR (handwritten)
price_note: Free, open-source model weights (MIT license). No usage fees. Cost is only your own compute/GPU. As of 2026-06, weights are downloaded from Hugging Face at no charge (base ~334M params, large ~558M params, small ~62M params). If served behind the Hugging Face Inference Providers/Endpoints, you pay that platform's compute rates, but the model itself is free.
best_for: High-accuracy recognition of English handwritten (cursive included) single text-line images when you already have line/word segmentation and want a free, self-hostable, MIT-licensed model. Ideal as the recognition stage in a custom handwriting pipeline (e.g. after a detector like CRAFT or a layout/line segmenter).

name: Unstructured.io API
license: Apache-2.0 (core OSS library); the hosted Serverless API and Platform are proprietary SaaS
price_note: As of 2026-06: hosted Serverless API is pay-as-you-go at $0.03/page (flat, regardless of file type or pipeline). Free plan includes 15,000 free pages with no expiration and full feature access. Business/Platform tier is custom (contact sales) and adds multi-user accounts and dedicated-instance/VPC deployment. The core `unstructured` Python library is free/open-source (Apache-2.0) and self-hostable at no cost.
best_for: RAG/LLM ingestion pipelines that need to turn heterogeneous documents (PDFs, scans, images, Office files, email, HTML) into clean, chunk-ready structured elements with layout, tables, and metadata — rather than pure raw-text OCR. Strong when you want one ETL layer feeding a vector store.

name: winocr (Windows OCR)
license: MIT (the Python binding); underlying Windows.Media.Ocr engine is proprietary and bundled with Windows
price_note: Free. The winocr Python package is MIT-licensed; the underlying Windows OCR engine ships with Windows 10/11 at no extra cost (requires a Windows OS license). No per-page or API fees, no metering. OCR language packs are free to install via Windows Settings. As of 2026-06.
best_for: Windows-only pipelines needing free, fully offline OCR of clean printed text (English/European Latin scripts, plus Japanese/Chinese/Korean) with zero per-page cost and no external dependencies. Good for batch local processing and for serving on-prem OCR to other machines via the bundled winocr_serve REST endpoint.

name: ABBYY Cloud OCR SDK / Document AI API (FineReader engine)
price_note: No public list pricing (as of 2026-06). Legacy Cloud OCR SDK (end-of-sale since 1 Jan 2023, no new customers): pre-purchased annual 'pages-limited' subscription, quote-based; third-party estimates put ABBYY per-page OCR around $0.02-$0.10/page depending on volume. Newer Document AI API (launched 15 Apr 2025, technical preview): self-service 'predictable pay-as-you-go' by document/credits, free sign-up with sandbox and trial credits, no credit card to start. Exact per-document price not published; contact docAI@abbyy.com.
best_for: High-accuracy enterprise document conversion at scale (image-only PDF/scans to searchable PDF, DOCX/XLSX, structured data) in 200+ languages, where a mature, compliance-friendly commercial vendor and field/key-value extraction (invoices, IDs, business cards, receipts) matter more than open-source/local control.

name: Adobe PDF Extract API (PDF Services)
price_note: As of 2026-06: Free tier = 500 Document Transactions/month. Paid is annual subscription only (no per-call pay-as-you-go). Published annual tiers: 25,000 transactions = $1,875; 75,000 = $5,250; 250,000 ≈ $16,250; 500,000 = $30,000; 750,000 = $41,250 — i.e. roughly $0.055–$0.075 per Document Transaction depending on volume. For Extract PDF / PDF-to-Markdown, 1 Document Transaction covers up to 5 pages (rounded up per 5 pages), so a 5-page scan = 1 transaction. Larger enterprise/volume contracts via Adobe sales.
best_for: Extracting clean structured content (text blocks, headings, reading order, tables to CSV/XLSX, figures) with bounding boxes from native or scanned business PDFs at moderate volume — especially RAG/LLM ingestion pipelines and table-heavy documents where layout fidelity matters more than non-English or math/handwriting support.

name: AWS Rekognition DetectText
price_note: As of 2026-06 (US East, Group 2 APIs tier that includes DetectText): tiered per-image — $0.0010/image for the first 1M images/month, $0.0008/image for the next 4M, $0.0006/image for the next 30M, and $0.00025/image beyond 35M images/month. I.e. roughly $1.00 per 1,000 images at low volume. Pricing varies slightly by region. AWS Free Tier: 1,000 images/month free for the first 12 months from account creation (shared across Group 1 and Group 2 image APIs). Note: as of July 15, 2025, new accounts instead get up to $200 in AWS Free Tier credits usable across eligible services for 6 months.
best_for: Reading short bursts of text from real-world photos and scenes — street signs, storefronts, product labels, license plates, T-shirts, screenshots, social/meme images — where you also want per-word/per-line bounding boxes and confidence scores. Good when you are already in the AWS ecosystem and need scene-text, not document parsing.

name: AWS Textract
price_note: As of 2026-06 (US East/US West Oregon, on-demand, per 1,000 pages, tier "first 1M pages/month"): Detect Document Text (raw OCR) $1.50; Tables $15.00; Forms (key-value) $50.00; Queries $15.00; Forms+Tables+Queries combined $70.00; Layout free when used with Tables; Signatures $3.50 (free add-on when used with another Analyze feature); Analyze Expense (invoices/receipts) $10.00; Analyze ID $25.00; Custom Queries $25.00; Analyze Lending $70.00. Volume discounts above 1M pages/month, e.g. Detect Document Text drops to $0.60, Tables $10.00, Forms $40.00, Analyze Expense $8.00, Analyze ID $10.00. No minimum fee or upfront commitment; pay only for what you process.
best_for: Teams already on AWS that need scalable, managed extraction of structured data (tables, form key-value pairs, invoices, receipts, US IDs) from English/Western-European documents, with bounding boxes and confidence scores for downstream validation — rather than just raw multilingual text dumps.

name: Azure AI Document Intelligence (formerly Form Recognizer)
price_note: Pay-as-you-go (US, S0 tier, as of 2026-06): Read OCR ~$1.50 per 1,000 pages (tiered down to ~$0.60/1k above 1M pages/month); Layout ~$10 per 1,000 pages; prebuilt models (Invoice, Receipt, ID, W-2, etc.) ~$10 per 1,000 pages; Custom extraction (neural/template) ~$30 per 1,000 pages (~$20/1k above 1M); Custom classification ~$3 per 1,000 pages. Add-on premium features (high-resolution, font, formula, barcode) ~$6 per 1,000 pages; Query fields ~$10 per 1,000 pages. Custom model training is free; blob storage billed separately. Figures vary by region and change over time; confirm on the official pricing page.
best_for: Production intelligent document processing on Azure where you need high-accuracy structured extraction: invoices, receipts, IDs/passports, US tax forms (W-2/1098/1099/1040), bank statements, pay stubs, mortgage forms, plus Layout (tables, selection marks, reading order, Markdown) and trainable custom extraction/classification models. Strong fit for regulated/enterprise workflows already in the Azure ecosystem, including on-prem via containers.

name: Azure AI Document Intelligence (Read OCR)
price_note: As of 2026-06: Read OCR (S0 paid tier) is $1.50 per 1,000 pages, with a volume tier dropping to ~$0.60 per 1,000 pages above 1M pages/month. Free (F0) tier: first 500 pages/month free, but caps each request to the first 2 pages of a document and 4 MB file size. (For comparison: Layout and most prebuilt models are $10/1,000 pages; custom extraction $50/1,000 pages.) Searchable-PDF output is included at no added cost.
best_for: Cloud-based, high-volume extraction of printed AND handwritten text from documents (PDFs, scans, images) where you need per-word confidence, bounding boxes, broad multilingual coverage, and optional searchable-PDF output — and where sending data to Azure (or running the licensed on-prem container) is acceptable.

name: Anthropic Claude Vision (Opus / Sonnet / Haiku)
price_note: As of June 2026, billed per token (not per page). Claude Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6: $5/MTok input, $25/MTok output. Claude Sonnet 4.6: $3/$15. Claude Haiku 4.5: $1/$5. PDF/image pages are billed as extracted-text tokens (~1,500-3,000/page) plus visual tokens (up to ~4,784/page on Opus 4.7+, ~1,568 on other models). Batch API: 50% off both directions; prompt-cache reads cost 0.1x base input. No fixed per-page OCR price.
best_for: Prompt-driven extraction from complex, mixed documents (financial reports, forms, contracts) where you want transcription plus reasoning/structuring (e.g. direct-to-JSON, table-to-markdown, chart Q&A) in one call, rather than raw layout-faithful OCR. Good when you also need handwriting, charts, and key-value extraction and can tolerate API/cloud usage.

name: Extend
price_note: As of 2026-06: credit-based, "you pay per page" via credits-per-page x plan per-credit rate. Pay As You Go tier starts free with 10,000 free credits to get started (per-credit rate drops at higher volume). Scale tier is $500/month including 50,000 credits/month with volume discounts. Enterprise is custom-quoted (adds self-hosted/BYOC, SSO/SAML/RBAC, custom rate limits). Example: extracting a 10-page doc on PAYG = 50 credits (5 credits/page). Exact dollar-per-credit not published on the public pricing page.
best_for: Production document-processing pipelines for regulated/complex-document industries (financial services, healthcare, logistics, real estate) that need parsing-to-markdown, structured field extraction, classification, and PDF splitting/editing with eval tooling, confidence flagging, and agentic schema refinement — rather than commodity plain-text OCR.

name: Google Gemini Vision (1.5 / 2.x / 3)
price_note: As of 2026-06, token-billed per the Gemini API pricing page. Representative paid-tier rates per 1M tokens: Gemini 2.5 Flash $0.30 in (text/image/video) / $2.50 out; Gemini 2.5 Pro $1.25 in (<=200k) / $10.00 out; Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite $0.10 in / $0.40 out; newer-generation Gemini 3.x/3.5 tiers (e.g. Gemini 3 Flash ~$0.50 in / $3.00 out, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview ~$2-4 in / $12-18 out) per the live pricing page. Images/PDF pages are billed as input tokens: a full image tile or PDF page ~258 tokens (images <=384px = 258 tokens; larger images split into 768x768 tiles at 258 tokens each). Batch mode gives ~50% discount. Prices change frequently; confirm on the pricing page.
best_for: Teams that want one API to do OCR plus understanding — extracting structured data (tables, key-value, JSON), transcribing handwriting/historical documents, reading math/charts, or converting PDFs to Markdown/LaTeX — over long multi-page documents, without standing up local infrastructure, and who can accept cloud processing and LLM non-determinism.

name: Google Cloud Vision (DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION)
price_note: As of 2026-06: DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION is billed at $1.50 per 1,000 units (images/pages) for units 1,001–5,000,000/month, and $0.60 per 1,000 units beyond 5,000,000/month. First 1,000 units/month are free. Each image or PDF/TIFF page counts as one unit per requested feature. Pricing is per Google Cloud project per month.
best_for: Production document and handwriting OCR at scale where a reliable, low-maintenance cloud API is acceptable: scanned forms, letters, notes, dense printed pages, and multilingual documents needing structured blocks/words with bounding boxes and confidence.

name: Google Cloud Document AI
price_note: As of 2026-06: Enterprise Document OCR $1.50/1,000 pages (1-5M pages/mo), $0.60/1,000 above 5M. Form Parser and Custom Extractor $30/1,000 pages (1-1M), $20/1,000 above 1M. Layout Parser $10/1,000 pages. Pretrained Invoice and Expense/Receipt parsers ~$0.10 per 10 pages; ID parsers (US Driver License, US Passport, Identity Document Proofing) ~$0.10 per document. Custom-model neural training ~$3/hour after first 10 free hours/month. Not billed for failed (4xx/5xx) requests.
best_for: Enterprises on Google Cloud needing managed, scalable OCR plus structured entity extraction from business documents (invoices, receipts, W2s, pay slips, bank statements, IDs, forms) with key-value pairs, tables, and reading order returned as structured JSON.

name: Google Cloud Vision API (TEXT_DETECTION & DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION)
price_note: As of 2026-06: TEXT_DETECTION and DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION are priced identically. First 1,000 units/month free; units 1,001-5,000,000/month at $1.50 per 1,000 units; units 5,000,001+/month at $0.60 per 1,000 units. One "unit" = one image (each page of a multi-page PDF/TIFF counts as a separate unit). Prices are USD; non-USD via Cloud SKUs.
best_for: General-purpose cloud OCR at scale: extracting printed text from photos/scans/signage (TEXT_DETECTION) and dense multi-page documents plus handwriting with block/paragraph/word structure and bounding boxes (DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION), across many languages and scripts, when you want a managed pay-as-you-go API and don't need on-prem.

name: OpenAI GPT-4o / GPT-4.1 Vision
price_note: As of 2026-06 (standard API tier): GPT-4o = $2.50/1M input tokens, $10.00/1M output tokens. GPT-4.1 = $2.00/1M input, $8.00/1M output. GPT-4.1 mini ~ $0.40/1M input, $1.60/1M output (cheapest vision-capable option). Images are billed as input tokens by resolution/detail (low ~85 tokens; high mode tiles into 512px patches), so cost is per-token not per-page; a full-page document image in 'high' detail is roughly 1k-3k input tokens. Batch API ~50% discount; cached input ~50-75% off. No per-page OCR price since there is no OCR endpoint.
best_for: Flexible document understanding where you need extraction + reasoning/structuring in one step (key-value extraction, table-to-JSON, summarizing scanned docs, handwriting, charts/infographics) rather than raw high-fidelity transcription. Good when you already use OpenAI and want zero-setup OCR via prompt with schema-constrained JSON output.

name: Klippa DocHorizon OCR API
price_note: No public per-page price list (as of 2026-06). Klippa's own FAQ states 'flexible pricing, including monthly subscriptions and pay-as-you-go options' — price scales with document volume, with high-volume discounts lowering per-document cost. Third-party listings estimate roughly $0.01-0.05 per page by document type, but Klippa does not confirm these publicly. A €25 free-credit self-service trial is available; full pricing is quote-based via the sales/contact form. (The legacy klippa.com/en/pricing URL now 404s after the Doxis rebrand; sign-up is at dochorizon.klippa.com/public/signup.)
best_for: Structured data extraction from business documents — receipts, invoices, IDs/passports, bank statements, contracts — where you need clean key-value JSON plus fraud detection, verification and GDPR masking, rather than raw full-page OCR. Strong fit for EU-based fintech/accounting/onboarding workflows in Latin-script languages.

name: LlamaParse
price_note: As of 2026-06: credit-based, 1,000 credits = $1.25 (same in North America and Europe). Per-page parse costs (v2 API tiers): Fast = 1 credit/page (~$0.00125), Cost-Effective = 3 credits/page (~$0.00375), Agentic = 10 credits/page (~$0.0125), Agentic Plus = 45 credits/page (~$0.056). Add-ons: layout extraction +3 credits/page; audio 3 credits/min; spreadsheets 1 credit/sheet. Subscription tiers: Free $0 (10K credits/mo), Starter $50/mo (40K credits, PAYG up to $500/mo), Pro $500/mo (400K credits, PAYG up to $5,000/mo), Enterprise custom.
best_for: Teams building RAG/agent pipelines on complex, visually rich documents (financial reports, scientific papers, invoices, insurance/healthcare forms) who want LLM-ready markdown/JSON without managing OCR infrastructure, and who can accept a cloud SaaS and tune the cost/accuracy tier per document.

name: Mathpix (Snip + Convert API)
price_note: As of 2026-06. Convert API (pay-as-you-go): images $0.002/image (0-1M), $0.0015/image (1M+); PDF pages $0.005/page (0-1M), $0.0035/page (1M+); live-stroke sessions free up to 1K then $0.01/session. One-time $19.99 API setup fee. Snip app: Free (10 PDF pages + 10 images/month, 2x with .edu email); Pro $4.99/mo or $49.90/yr (1,000 PDF pages + 5,000 images/month); Organization $9.99/mo for 2 users ($4.49/mo per extra user, $3.99 at 50+). On-prem/SCS self-hosted container is custom enterprise pricing.
best_for: Digitizing STEM content — math/physics equations, chemistry structures, scientific tables, and handwritten notes — into LaTeX, Markdown, or DOCX, whether interactively via the Snip app or programmatically via the Convert API for document-processing pipelines.

name: Mindee
price_note: As of 2026-06: Free plan = 250 pages/month, no credit card required. Paid subscriptions (billed annually, ~10% discount): Starter EUR 44/mo (500 credits/mo, overage EUR 0.05/credit); Pro EUR 179/mo (2,500 credits/mo, overage EUR 0.04/credit); Business EUR 584/mo (10,000 credits/mo, overage EUR 0.035/credit); Enterprise = custom quote (~250,000+ credits/year). Effective pay-as-you-go rate ranges from ~USD 0.10/page at low volume down to ~USD 0.01/page at high volume. 1 credit = 1 physical page submitted (a 5-page doc = 5 credits), regardless of document type or complexity. A 14-day free trial of paid features is also offered.
best_for: Teams that want fast, training-free structured-JSON extraction from business documents (invoices, receipts, IDs, bank statements, payslips, contracts) via a hosted API, with prebuilt endpoints plus custom/generated models and a generous 250-page/month free tier — and who are comfortable sending documents to a cloud service.

name: Mistral OCR API (Document AI)
price_note: As of 2026-06: OCR text extraction $2 per 1,000 pages (~500 pages/$1); $1 per 1,000 pages with the Batch API (50% discount). Document annotation / structured-output extraction is billed separately at $3 per 1,000 pages. Vertex AI and Azure AI Foundry billing is metered through those clouds at the partner-model rate. No standing free OCR allowance; la Plateforme offers limited free experimentation credits/quotas for new accounts but no dedicated perpetual free OCR tier.
best_for: High-volume, low-cost conversion of PDFs and scanned/photographed documents (invoices, forms, reports, contracts) into structured Markdown + JSON for RAG pipelines and downstream LLM agents — especially when you need tables, math, multilingual text, and handwriting handled by a single commodity-priced API without managing GPUs.

name: OCR.space OCR API
price_note: As of 2026-06: Free tier $0. PRO $30/month (300,000 requests/mo, 5 MB file limit). PRO PDF $60/month (300,000 requests/mo, ~100 MB files, 999+ PDF pages). Enterprise custom (commonly cited starting ~$999/month) adds on-premise/self-hosted deployment, custom OCR tuning, guaranteed 100% uptime, and priority support. Engine 3 has its own separate quotas (~2,500 free / ~30,000 PRO monthly).
best_for: Quick, low-cost extraction of plain text from clean printed images and small multipage PDFs, generating searchable ("sandwich") PDFs, and prototyping — where a generous free tier and a zero-install REST call matter more than enterprise-grade accuracy, layout fidelity, or field-level extraction.

name: Pen2Txt
price_note: As of 2026-06 (EUR, monthly subscription, credit-based; ~1 credit = 1 page of handwritten text): Free trial = 3 credits (no card). Base = EUR 14.90/mo (100 credits). Premium = EUR 29.90/mo (250 credits). Enterprise = EUR 49.90/mo (500 credits). Month-to-month, no long-term commitment; unused credits do not roll over.
best_for: Individuals and small teams (students, researchers, professionals) digitizing handwritten notes, letters, journals, and forms — especially cursive or mixed cursive/print in common Latin or CJK languages — who also want built-in correction, summarization, and translation, and who do not need an API or offline processing.

name: Reducto
price_note: As of 2026-06: credit-based. Standard plan is pay-as-you-go at $0.015/credit (i.e. $15 per 1,000 credits; $1 buys ~67 credits). Parse costs 1 credit/page (standard) or 2 credits/page (complex); Agentic Parse 2 credits/page (standard) or 4 credits/page (complex); advanced chart agent +4 credits/chart; text files (HTML/TXT/RTF) 0.5 credits/page; spreadsheets 1 credit per 1,000 cells (accurate) or per 5,000 cells (fast). Extract 2 credits/page (Deep Extract 4 credits/page + 0.1/field, 30-credit minimum/doc); Split 2 (Deep Split 4) credits/page; Classify 0.5 credits/page (reads first 5 pages by default = 2.5 credits/classification); Edit 4 credits/page. Effective floor ~$0.015/page for simple Parse. Growth/Enterprise tiers are custom-priced with volume discounts.
best_for: Enterprise teams (finance, insurance, healthcare) parsing high volumes of ugly real-world PDFs — complex/merged-cell tables, scanned and handwritten forms, financial statements — into LLM-ready structured JSON/markdown, with VPC/on-prem and HIPAA options.

name: Taggun Receipt OCR
price_note: As of 2026-06 (USD): Developer $28/mo (500 scans, ~$0.056/scan), Startup $99/mo (1,800 scans), Business $399/mo (8,000 scans, $0.050/scan), Advanced $799/mo (20,000 scans, $0.040/scan), Enterprise custom. Overage ~$0.060–$0.040/scan by tier. ~10% discount on annual billing. 30-day free trial (unlimited scans, no charge if cancelled in trial).
best_for: Production receipt and invoice data extraction at scale — expense management, loyalty/rewards validation, and receipt fraud detection — where you want a turnkey API that returns structured fields (total, tax, date, merchant, line items, tax IDs) rather than raw OCR text.

name: Upstage Document Parse / Document OCR
price_note: As of 2026-06: Document Parse Standard $0.01/page, Enhanced $0.03/page, Auto mode selects Standard/Enhanced per page. Standalone Document OCR endpoint $0.0015/page. Prices exclude 10% VAT. Prepaid-credit bonus tiers scale with monthly commitment (Explore $100+/mo +10%, Build $500+/mo +15%, Scale $5,000+/mo +20%; higher yearly bonuses up to ~+40%). Self-hosted via AWS Marketplace SageMaker listings billed per instance-hour (not flat): standard Document Parse ~$10/hour real-time and ~$15/hour batch (instance-dependent); Document Parse Enhanced ~$12/hour real-time (ml.g6.12xlarge); plus underlying AWS infrastructure costs. New users get free sign-up credits and Upstage Studio agents include 10 free runs with no credit card (no permanent free tier).
best_for: RAG ingestion and LLM-ready conversion of complex, layout-heavy business documents (PDFs, scans, slides, spreadsheets) into clean HTML/Markdown — especially when Korean/CJK content, complex/multi-page tables, charts, or forms are involved.

name: Veryfi OCR API
price_note: As of 2026-06 (USD): Free plan = 100 documents/month, $0. Starter plan (0-25,000 docs/mo) = $500/month minimum, billed per document: receipts $0.08, invoices with line items $0.16 (other doc types higher, e.g. bank checks/statements ~$0.25, W-2/W-9 ~$0.16). $500 minimum covers ~6,250 receipts or ~3,125 invoices/month. Custom/volume plan for 25,000+ docs/mo with volume discounts and no monthly minimum (contact sales@veryfi.com). 12-month commitment adds ~$0.01/document discount. Billed monthly in advance; non-USD converted at exchange rates. An API transaction = one document of up to 15 pages.
best_for: High-volume, structured extraction of receipts and invoices (line items, taxes, tips, vendor, totals) into JSON, plus other financial documents (bank checks/statements, W-2/W-9, business cards) — for expense management, accounts payable, and fintech where pre-trained "Day 1" models and near real-time API throughput matter more than self-hosting.
